thesis: Arista is the merchant-silicon leader in high-speed data center Ethernet, riding the AI back-end networking wave as hyperscalers standardize on Ethernet over InfiniBand. FY2025 revenue grew 28.6% to $9.0B with 64% gross margins, ~43% operating margins, and ~$4B free cash flow on a debt-free balance sheet. Q1 2026 accelerated to +35% YoY and management targets $11.5B revenue and $3.5B of AI networking revenue in 2026. At ~58x trailing earnings the multiple is full but supported by durable growth, elite profitability, and a dominant AI-Ethernet position; customer concentration (Microsoft ~26%, Meta ~16%) is the key risk.

drivers: AI back-end networking revenue exceeds the $3.5B 2026 target as Ethernet displaces InfiniBand
Campus and enterprise expansion diversifies revenue beyond cloud titans
800G and emerging 1.6T Ethernet cycle drives sustained port and ASP growth
Operating margins hold above 42% and buybacks compound EPS on ~$4B+ FCF

base_case.assumptions: Revenue grows ~25–30% to ~$11.5B in 2026 then ~$14B in 2027; gross margins stay 62–64%; operating margins near 42%; the market applies ~48–52x forward earnings on ~$4.00 of 2027 EPS.

risks: Hyperscaler AI capex digestion cuts orders and compresses the multiple toward 30–35x
Microsoft or Meta shift spend to white-box or in-house switching, hitting concentrated revenue
InfiniBand or competing Ethernet fabrics from Nvidia, Cisco and Broadcom-based OEMs erode share
Gross-margin pressure from mix shift toward large cloud deals and tariff-driven component costs

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings — consensus ~$0.89 EPS on ~$2.83B revenue; AI networking progress vs $3.5B target
Q3 2026 earnings and updated 2027 revenue framework (Street ~$14B)
800G Ethernet ramp and initial 1.6T design wins at top hyperscalers
Q4 and full-year 2026 results — confirmation of ~$11.5B revenue and AI mix

key_risks: Customer concentration: Microsoft ~26% and Meta ~16% of revenue (~42% combined)
Valuation: ~58x trailing earnings prices in continued hypergrowth
AI capex cycle sensitivity — a hyperscaler spending pause would hit orders hard
Competition from Nvidia (InfiniBand/Spectrum-X), Cisco, and white-box Ethernet
Gross-margin dilution from concentrated large-cloud deals and component/tariff costs
